The test image shows soybean pods with large, irregular dark brown/purple-black blotches covering significant portions of the pod surface, with some pinkish areas. This points toward pod-affecting diseases.

Top candidates:
- **Anthracnose**: irregular dark spots on pods with acervuli
- **Cercospora**: reddish-purple lesions on pods

Let me check the Anthracnose reference image.

The reference Anthracnose image shows irregular dark gray-black blotches on pods — the same pattern of irregular dark lesions seen on the test image's pods (though the test pods are still green/fresh while the reference is dried).

Key matching features:
- Irregular dark blotches on pod surfaces
- Pattern of large, coalescing dark areas
- The test image also shows pinkish areas consistent with early acervuli development

The irregular, non-angular coalescing lesions and pod-focused symptom presentation align with Anthracnose rather than Cercospora (which would show more purple/reddish coloring) or Diaporthe/Phomopsis (which show linear rows of pycnidia or affect seed quality more directly)."}
